shared.region: DP table, scrolls sideways when wider than the screen
shared.legendRead: Dashed border: a cell it reads

dpRow.legendHouses: Above: the value of each house, v[i - 1] above best[i].
dpRow.legendInf: INF = amount + 1, more than any answer: the amount is not made yet.

stairs.start: ways[i] is the number of ways to reach step i. Base cases: ways[0] = ways[1] = 1.
stairs.step: The last move to step {{i}} was 1 step, from {{a}}, or 2 steps, from {{b}}: {{formula}}.
stairs.hint: A whole number from 1 to {{max}}, so the row fits. (The problem allows n up to 90.)

house.start: best[i] is the largest total using only the first i houses. Base cases: best[0] = 0 and best[1] = {{first}}, the first house.
house.take: House {{i}} ({{v}}): skip it, {{skip}}, or take it, {{take}}. Taking it is larger: {{result}}.
house.skip: House {{i}} ({{v}}): skip it, {{skip}}, or take it, {{take}}. Skipping it is larger: {{result}}.
house.tie: House {{i}} ({{v}}): skip it, {{skip}}, or take it, {{take}}. Both are equal: {{result}}.
house.hint: 1 to {{max}} whole numbers from 0 to 99, separated by spaces or commas. (The problem allows up to 1000 houses.)
house.invalid: Use whole numbers from 0 to 99, separated by spaces or commas.

coins.start: best[x] is the fewest coins making amount x. best[0] = 0; every other amount starts at INF = {{inf}} (amount + 1), more than any answer.
coins.better: Amount {{x}}, coin {{c}}: {{expr}}, smaller than the best so far, {{old}}: {{result}}.
coins.notBetter: Amount {{x}}, coin {{c}}: {{expr}}, not smaller than the best so far, {{old}}: best[{{x}}] stays {{old}}.
coins.fromInf: Amount {{x}}, coin {{c}}: best[{{r}}] is INF, so amount {{r}} cannot be made and this coin cannot finish {{x}}: best[{{x}}] stays {{old}}.
coins.noCoin: Amount {{x}}: no coin is at most {{x}}, so best[{{x}}] stays INF.
coins.none: best[{{x}}] is still INF: amount {{x}} cannot be made. Print -1.
coins.hint: 1 to {{maxCoins}} different coin values from 1 to {{maxValue}}, and an amount from 0 to {{maxAmount}}, so the row fits. (The problem allows amounts up to 10000.)
coins.coinsInvalid: Use 1 to {{maxCoins}} different whole numbers from 1 to {{maxValue}}, separated by spaces or commas.
coins.amountInvalid: The amount must be a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.

dpTable.labelBack: Tracing back at {{cell}}; path so far: {{path}}.
dpTable.legendPath: •: on the path traced back from the answer
dpTable.legendGrid: Small numbers outside: i and j. Row 0 and column 0 are the extra zeros; p[0][1] = 1.
dpTable.legendKnapsack: Columns: the capacity w. Rows: the items as (weight, value); row 0 has none.
dpTable.legendStrings: Rows: the letters of A; columns: the letters of B; - is row 0 or column 0.

grid.start: The table has an extra row and column of zeros, and p[0][1] = 1 seeds the start. A cell is entered from above or from the left: p[i][j] = p[i - 1][j] + p[i][j - 1]; a blocked cell has 0.
grid.step: From above plus from the left: {{formula}}.
grid.hint: 1 to {{max}} rows of 1 to {{max}} characters, each . (free) or # (blocked), separated by spaces or commas. Start at the top-left, goal at the bottom-right. (The problem allows up to 30 by 30.)
grid.onlyDots: Use only . and # in each row, and separate rows with spaces or commas.

knapsack.start: best(i, w) is the best value using only the first i items with capacity w. Row 0 has no items: 0 everywhere.
knapsack.noFit: Item {{item}} does not fit in w = {{w}}: leave it out, {{result}}.
knapsack.take: Item {{item}}, w = {{w}}: without it {{without}}, with it {{with}}. Take it: {{result}}.
knapsack.skip: Item {{item}}, w = {{w}}: without it {{without}}, with it {{with}}. Leave it out: {{result}}.
knapsack.tie: Item {{item}}, w = {{w}}: without it {{without}}, with it {{with}}. Both are equal: {{result}}.
knapsack.hint: 1 to {{maxItems}} items separated by commas, each a weight from 1 to {{max}} and a value from 0 to 99 separated by a space, and a capacity from 1 to {{max}}. (The problem allows 100 items and a capacity of 10000.)
knapsack.itemsInvalid: Use 1 to {{maxItems}} items separated by commas, each a weight from 1 to {{max}} and a value from 0 to 99, for example 1 15, 3 20.
knapsack.capacityInvalid: The capacity must be a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.

strings.hint: 0 to {{max}} letters a to z in each, as in the problem (either may be empty). (The problem allows {{limit}} letters.)
strings.invalid: Use only the letters a to z, at most {{max}} in each string.

lcs.start: L[i][j] is the LCS length of the first i letters of A and the first j of B. Row 0 and column 0 are 0.
lcs.differ: {{x}} ≠ {{y}}: take the larger of up and left: {{formula}}.
lcs.answer: {{cell}} = {{value}} is the LCS length. Now trace back from it to find the letters.
lcs.backEqual: At {{cell}}: equal letters, so {{letter}} is in the subsequence. Go diagonally to {{next}}.
lcs.backUp: At {{cell}}: {{x}} ≠ {{y}}, and up ({{up}}) is at least left ({{left}}). Go up to {{next}}.
lcs.backLeft: At {{cell}}: {{x}} ≠ {{y}}, and left ({{left}}) is larger than up ({{up}}). Go left to {{next}}.
lcs.end: {{cell}} is on row 0 or column 0, so the trace ends. The common subsequence is {{found}}, of length {{value}}. Print {{value}}.
lcs.endEmpty: {{cell}} is on row 0 or column 0, so the trace ends. The common subsequence is empty. Print 0.

edit.start: D[i][j] is the fewest operations turning the first i letters of A into the first j of B. Row 0 and column 0 are the base cases: i deletes or j inserts.
edit.equal: {{x}} = {{y}}: the diagonal is free. Diagonal {{diag}}, up (delete) {{up}}, left (insert) {{left}}: {{result}}.
edit.answer: {{cell}} = {{value}} is the edit distance. Now trace back from it to find the operations.
edit.backKeep: At {{cell}}: {{x}} = {{y}}, keep it (free). Go diagonally to {{next}}.
edit.backReplace: At {{cell}}: replace {{x}} with {{y}}. Go diagonally to {{next}}.
edit.end: The trace has reached D[0][0]. The operations: {{ops}}. Print {{value}}.
edit.endNone: The trace has reached D[0][0] with no operation: A and B are equal. Print 0.
